title: Story of the Limping Schoolmaster

full_text:
The third teacher of the academy, Master Kamil, walked with a noticeable limp, leaning upon a polished pearwood cane.
He smiled at the gathered youths: 'Since my brothers have confessed their follies, let me complete the trio with the tale of my stubborn foot!

In my youth, I was an impatient copyist who hated copying long manuscripts line by line. I was constantly seeking shortcuts to wealth.
One day, an eccentric alchemist told me that on the highest ledge of the Citadel cliffs, there grew a rare wild herb whose juice, when mixed with ink, would write letters of pure gold.

Instead of taking the winding, paved road that climbed safely to the summit, I reasoned: "Why walk three miles around the mountain when I can climb the sheer rock face in twenty minutes?"

I began scaling the crumbling limestone precipice. Halfway up, with the city roofs spread far below, I reached for a tuft of green weeds growing out of a rock fissure.
The moment my fingers closed around the weed, the rock ledge crumbled beneath my sandals!

I tumbled down twenty cubits, bouncing off thorny brambles, until I landed hard in an olive orchard, snapping my ankle bone into splinters!

When the bone-setter finished binding my leg, he looked at the crushed weeds still clutched in my bruised hand. He laughed and said:
"Young fool! This is not an alchemical herb; it is ordinary bitter spurge, which even goats refuse to eat!"

My ankle healed crookedly, leaving me with this eternal limp. But that stumble was the greatest blessing of my life. It taught me that there are no magic shortcuts in life—neither to knowledge, nor to wealth, nor to virtue.
Since then, I walk slowly upon the paved road of patient study, teaching you boys that slow, steady steps upon the right path always outstrip the reckless leaps of vanity.'
moral: Greed for shortcuts brings a heavy stumble; the straight path of honest patience leads safely home.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Story of the Limping Schoolmaster"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
